memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: And he said, "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree that I commanded you not to eat from?" The man said, "The woman you put here with me — she gave me some fruit from the tree, and I ate it." — Gen 3:11–12 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
God asks two searching questions, gently leading Adam toward honest confession. "Who told you that you were naked? Have you eaten from the tree?" There is space here for Adam simply to say, "Yes, Lord. I did. I'm sorry." But that is not what happens.

Instead, Adam points the finger. "The woman you put here with me — she gave me the fruit." In one short sentence he manages to blame both his wife and, astonishingly, God Himself. The gift of a companion, once his joy (Gen 2:23), is now recast as the source of his downfall. Notice how little "I ate it" there is, and how much blame surrounds it.

This is the sad reflex of a sinful heart — to protect ourselves by pushing the fault onto someone else. We would rather explain our sin than own it. But blame never heals us; it only keeps us hiding behind new fig leaves of excuse.

Dear friend, God does not need our excuses. He is not looking for someone to blame, but for a heart willing to come clean. And the wonder of the Gospel is that we can. Because Jesus took full responsibility for sins that were never His, we are free to take honest responsibility for sins that are ours — knowing that when we confess, He faithfully forgives (1 Jn 1:9).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. When confronted with your own wrong, do you tend to confess it or explain it away?
2. Is there someone — or even God — you have quietly blamed for your own choices?
3. What would it look like to simply say "I did it" before God this week?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, forgive me for how quickly I make excuses and shift the blame instead of owning my sin. Thank You that Jesus took the blame He never deserved so that I could be forgiven. Give me a humble and honest heart that comes clean before You. Amen.
